haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes for one order. If not claimed in time, Inventory drops it by itself and sends no message.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Stock is reserved before any payment is requested. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and status becomes Out of stock.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is the idempotency key on every charge. A repeat with the same key is treated as the same request, so the customer is never charged twice.
haiku-low.q4: Payment refunds the full amount to the provider. Order sets Refund pending until the refund is confirmed, then Out of stock, and emails the customer that it is cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q5: Only after the order is confirmed, on OrderConfirmed. If checkout fails, the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED. The document names no coordinator. Order keeps the order status in its own database.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment saves the outcome and publishes PaymentOutcome on the shared message broker, which Order and Inventory act on.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks whether it has already seen the webhook event id and ignores repeats. Claim and release are also safe to repeat for the same order id.
haiku-low.q9: Inventory releases the reservation, triggered by the PaymentOutcome event saying declined. Order also sets status Declined.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory tries to claim the reservation. If the claim works, Order confirms. If the reservation has lapsed, the payment is refunded.
haiku-low.q11: Payment keeps retrying the refund. The refund record stays Refund pending in the Payment database and is never deleted. Alerting time is not decided.
haiku-low.q12: Order publishes OrderConfirmed once the claim succeeds. Cart receives it and empties the customer's cart, retrying until acknowledged.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, Inventory drops it by itself and sends no message.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before any payment is requested. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment, order status Out of stock and the customer is told which items.
sonnet.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key on every charge; a repeat with the same key is treated as the same request, so the provider does not charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Payment refunds the full amount to the provider (refund status Refund pending until confirmed); once the refund succeeds the order becomes Out of stock (cancelled) and the customer is emailed.
sonnet.q5: Emptied only after the order is confirmed (Cart empties on OrderConfirmed). On any failure the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED as a single component. Steps are driven by events (PaymentOutcome, OrderConfirmed) and requests between services; Order keeps the order status in its own database, but no overall checkout progress record/orchestrator is named.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which saves the outcome and publishes a PaymentOutcome event on the message broker; Order and Inventory act on that event.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores each webhook event id and ignores (replies OK to) any webhook whose event id it has seen. Also claim and release are safe to repeat for the same order id when the broker redelivers.
sonnet.q9: The PaymentOutcome event (Declined) triggers Order to set status Declined and Inventory to release the reservation; if release fails, it expires after 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: Inventory tries to claim the reservation: if the claim works the order is Confirmed; if the reservation has lapsed the claim fails and the design refunds (no re-reserving).
sonnet.q11: Payment keeps retrying; the refund record stays Refund pending and is never deleted, tracked in the Payment database (refund record), with Order status Refund pending in the Order database.
sonnet.q12: Order publishing the OrderConfirmed event; the Cart service empties the cart (redelivered until Cart acknowledges).
